learning_outcomes.text: Students who have successfully completed this module will have a basic knowledge of light generation, vision, color definition and color perception. They know different light sources and luminaire systems and have basic knowledge of lighting design and central lighting standards.

Students can verbally describe color and light phenomena and assign them to physical models according to their complexity. They have basic knowledge of the materialization and shaping of visible light.

Students are able to perceive and describe properties and characteristics of existing natural or artificially generated lighting and lighting designs, as well as their effects on the recipients of the design solutions.

Students can report on lighting in environments and rooms using subject-specific terminology and discuss them in a target-group-specific manner. They can pre-visualize and simulate simple concepts and verbally represent them. They can organize corresponding collaboration among themselves on the non-linguistic field of light experience and present their work results comparatively.

assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a written exam, the scope of which is defined by the currently valid study regulations. The ungraded assessment is experimental work, consisting of approximately 5 laboratory experiments of 90 minutes each.
